Hi Morgan — great speaking with you. This matches my notes; below is a concise recap plus the cost levers and a proposed short path for procurement and kickoff.

Recap (short):
- Target: p95 <= 120ms for real-time scoring flow (1K req/s spikes) while keeping pilot budget under $15k/month.
- Key constraints: bursty traffic (short 10–30s spikes), mix of short prompts (8–40 tokens) and occasional long context (200–400 tokens), need for regression guardrails.

Primary cost & performance levers we can test in pilot:
1) Batching: continuous micro-batching for queued scoring plus adaptive batching for burst windows. Expected improvement: 25–45% token-cost reduction for short prompts.
2) KV prefix caching: store common user/context tokens to avoid re-computation on repeated requests (esp. for returning users). Expected: up to 30% fewer decode tokens in practice on retention-heavy cohorts.
3) Quantized model variants (8-bit/4-bit): lower GPU memory and faster kernel paths; tradeoff test for quality + latency. Expected: 20–50% per-token cost reduction depending on model.
4) Model routing: route low-latency traffic to a trimmed, faster model; batch background scoring on higher quality model. Expected: predictable p95 by isolation.

Quick example token-econ snapshot (pilot estimate, ballpark):
- Baseline (current): 15M tokens/month -> $12,000/month (hosted endpoint, no batching)
- With batching + caching: 12M effective tokens -> $8,400/month (-30%)
- + quantized inference on dedicated GPUs: $6,300/month (-47% vs baseline)

Proposed pilot scope (6 weeks):
Week 0: SOW + security questionnaire + dataset access
Week 1–2: Integration + baseline metrics collection (latency, token counts, distribution)
Week 3–4: Deploy batching + prefix caching + quantized variants; run A/B and quality checks
Week 5: SLO validation & regression runbook; stakeholder demo
Week 6: Economics review and recommendations + procurement-ready pricing

What we need from FinTechX this week:
- Example traffic trace (1–2 days) and representative prompts (redacted is fine)
- Point of contact for procurement (you mentioned procurement@fintechx.com)
- Security questionnaire owner for SOC2 checklist responses

Next steps I’ll take:
- I’m attaching a short pilot proposal and a token-econ runsheet that our Solutions team will fill with concrete numbers once we ingest traces.
- Schedule a 30-min kickoff with solutions + infra: I propose Thurs 24 Jun 10:00–10:30 PT. If that works I’ll send calendar invites.

If you’re good with this, I’ll loop in Laura (solutions engineering) and Neha (AE) to prepare pricing and the SOW.

Best,
